around.headline: Bengaluru bus passenger offers tea to elderly woman, steals her gold chain
around.summary: A fellow passenger allegedly offered an elderly woman tea on a Bengaluru bus and then stole her gold chain, per TOI Bengaluru. Never accept food or drink from strangers while travelling alone, and keep jewellery covered on public transport.

around.headline: Wild elephant tramples morning walker to death near BM Kaval forest
around.summary: An elderly man was killed by a wild elephant during his morning walk near BM Kaval forest close to Bengaluru, per Deccan Herald and The Times of India. Avoid solo walks on forest-fringe stretches at dawn and dusk.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Spurious drugs racket kingpin arrested at Bengaluru airport after landing from Sharjah
around.summary: The alleged kingpin of the fake medicine racket was held at Bengaluru airport after a month-long manhunt, per The Hindu and ThePrint. Buy medicines only from licensed pharmacies and check the batch number and manufacturer on the strip.

around.headline: Sudden downpour brings Bengaluru traffic to a crawl; IT corridor waterlogged
around.summary: Heavy rain caused waterlogging and long jams, especially on the IT corridor, per Deccan Herald and NDTV. With more rain forecast today, allow extra time and avoid low-lying underpasses.

around.headline: Namma BMTC App 2.0 launched with integrated bus and metro ticketing; KSRTC to start Rajahamsa service to Bhagamandala from Oct 1
around.summary: BMTC's upgraded app combines bus and metro ticketing, per This Week India. Separately, KSRTC will run a new Rajahamsa service from Bengaluru to Bhagamandala in Kodagu from October 1, per Deccan Herald.

around.headline: Residents symbolically 'open' Metro Pink Line, demand early launch
around.summary: Locals held a symbolic ribbon-cutting for the Pink Line out of frustration with delays, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald; Construction World reports it is moving closer to an October opening. Don't plan your commute around it until BMRCL announces an official date.

around.headline: Mekedatu project cost jumps 86% to Rs 16.7k crore as state awaits Centre's nod
around.summary: The Mekedatu drinking-water project's estimated cost has risen sharply while Karnataka waits for the Centre's approval, per TOI Bengaluru. Bengaluru's water supply depends heavily on the Kaveri, so the delay matters to residents.

events.name: International Coffee Day celebrations
events.note: Bengaluru will mark International Coffee Day on October 1, per kodaguexpress.com — look out for cafe tastings and events.

events.name: Literary festival on Karnataka's indigenous languages
events.note: Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan hosts the festival as part of its 60th anniversary events in Bengaluru, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald.

events.name: AgriCon–HortiConnect India 2026
events.note: An agriculture and horticulture trade event in Bengaluru with drones and farm machinery on show, per Deccan Herald — mainly for buyers and industry visitors.

street_smart.title: You're on a Bengaluru bus alone when the friendly passenger beside you offers you tea from his flask, saying he has 'extra' and you look tired. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: TOI Bengaluru: 'Bengaluru bus passenger offers tea to elderly woman, steals gold chain' (2026-09-29).
street_smart.situation: He's polite, chatty and says he's going the same way. Your stop is 40 minutes away and you're wearing a gold chain and carrying a bag.

choices.text: Accept — refusing would be rude, and he's drinking from the same flask.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Thieves offer food or drink precisely because refusal feels impolite; the sharing-from-the-same-flask show builds trust while a sedative can be pre-mixed or added out of sight. Once you're drowsy, jewellery and bags are easy to take, and you may not remember what happened.

choices.text: Take a small sip only to be polite, and keep your bag on your lap.
choices.feedback: Even a small amount of a spiked drink can cause dizziness and confusion, and you can't taste most sedatives. Politeness isn't worth the risk.

choices.text: Politely decline, keep the chain covered, stay alert and move near the conductor or other passengers if he keeps insisting.
choices.feedback: A firm, friendly 'no thanks' costs nothing. Staying near the crew and other passengers removes the isolation these thefts rely on, and covering jewellery reduces the temptation.

choices.text: Say nothing, pretend to sleep so he stops talking.
choices.feedback: Sleeping makes you an easier target on the bus, whether or not he's the thief. Stay awake and aware instead.

takeaways: Never accept food, drinks or sweets from strangers while travelling alone, however friendly they seem.
Cover gold jewellery and keep bags on your lap or in front of you on public transport.
If you feel drowsy or robbed, alert the conductor/driver and call the police on 112; for women in distress on a bus, tell the crew immediately.

quiz.question: A wild elephant killed a morning walker near BM Kaval forest, on which Bengaluru road?
quiz.why: BM Kaval lies in Bengaluru South along Mysuru Road. Elephants moving out of forest fringes are most active at dawn and dusk.

quiz.question: KSRTC's new Rajahamsa service from October 1 connects Bengaluru with Bhagamandala in which district?
quiz.why: Bhagamandala is famous for the Triveni Sangam, where the Kaveri, Kannike and the underground Sujyoti meet.

quiz.question: The Mekedatu project, whose cost has jumped to Rs 16.7k crore, is on which river?
quiz.why: Mekedatu, meaning 'goat's leap', is a gorge on the Kaveri, and the project is meant mainly for Bengaluru's drinking water.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
quiz.why: Oxygen is only about 21%. Argon is the third most abundant at roughly 0.9%.

quiz.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
quiz.why: Appointments are made by the President on the recommendation of a selection committee under the 2023 law; the CEC's removal follows the process for a Supreme Court judge.
